drug_class: Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) — combination antiretroviral
purpose: This medicine is used to treat HIV infection in adults and children. It helps control the virus so your immune system can stay stronger and healthier. It does not cure HIV, but it helps keep the virus at very low levels in your body.
how_it_works: HIV is a virus that tries to copy itself inside your body's cells. This medication works by blocking a key tool the virus needs to make copies of itself, called reverse transcriptase. By blocking this tool, the medicine helps stop the virus from spreading and multiplying in your body.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, tiredness, dizziness, and trouble sleeping are the most common side effects. Some people may feel generally unwell when they first start taking it. These effects often get better after the first few weeks.
warnings: This medicine can rarely cause a serious buildup of lactic acid in the blood, which can be life-threatening — tell your doctor right away if you feel very weak, have stomach pain, trouble breathing, or feel cold and dizzy. It can also cause liver problems, including liver swelling. If you have hepatitis B, stopping this medicine suddenly can make hepatitis B worse. Never stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet taken by mouth twice a day, once in the morning and once at night. Each tablet contains lamivudine 150 mg and zidovudine 300 mg. It can be taken with or without food. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and try not to miss any doses.
